decisions.claim: Telling the user to sudo npm install into /usr/local contradicts G1's single privileged step
decisions.reason: REJECTED on the security merits. The reviewer's implied alternative - accept the home path and bind-mount it back past ProtectHome - is worse than the problem: a directory under the user's home is writable by everything running as that user, agents included, so the daemon would execute code its own agents can replace. That hands over the process guarding the credentials, not just the credentials. G1 scopes what the INSTALLER does; where the package itself lives is a separate, pre-existing choice. Kept the refusal and added the reasoning to the message so nobody 'fixes' it later.

decisions.claim: Migration shreds the legacy store even when the old daemon was not stopped, and a rerun cannot repair it
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED at migrate.ts:269-271 - the shred ran unconditionally after recording oldUnitStopped. Exactly the failure round 11's F4 was meant to close, reopened one line lower. The shred is now conditional, an unverifiable stop (no user bus, empty output) counts as still-running rather than success, and describe() prints the two commands that finish the job.

decisions.claim: Migration keeps an existing token file without checking its contents match the registered token
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. My round-11 fix repaired the token file's MODE and ignored its CONTENTS, so a stale token was chmodded to 0600 and the agent locked out permanently after the store was shredded. Now rewritten whenever it disagrees with the token being registered.

decisions.claim: registerProfile starts the credential socket before confirming the store was saved
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. Fixed more thoroughly than reported: saving before publishing was not enough, because the in-memory list was already rewritten and the previous socket closed by the time saveProfiles() threw - a rejected enrolment still took a working agent off the air. The unreadable-store check now runs before any mutation.

decisions.claim: maxConnections = 64 lets an unauthenticated process exclude the valid agent
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED, and it was MY regression from round 11: the ceiling I added to bound held connections became a second way to deny the real agent, one layer below the one I had just removed. setTimeout is an inactivity timeout, so a byte every few seconds held a slot indefinitely. The ceiling is gone; an absolute per-connection deadline bounds the resource instead, so slots cannot be held and need not be rationed.

decisions.claim: My own test called systemctl --user disable --now on the REAL wundervault-agent.service and stopped the developer's live daemon
decisions.reason: Not a reviewer finding - found by running the suite. The unit name was hardcoded, so the test did the real thing. Daemon restored (active + enabled, store intact and never touched). The unit name is now injectable via WUNDERVAULT_OLD_UNIT, the suite pins it to a non-existent unit, and a full run has been verified to leave the live service alone. Same class as the os.homedir() accident this file already carried a comment about: anything reaching outside the process has to be redirectable or it cannot be tested without doing it for real.
